short: The first empire on which the sun never set, financed by American silver.
full:
Columbus made landfall in 1492 and the Treaty of Tordesillas two years later gave Castile a claim to most of the Americas. Cortes and Pizarro took over the Aztec and Inca states in the 1520s and 1530s, inheriting populations already organised to pay tribute. The silver mountain at Potosi, worked from 1545, paid for Habsburg armies in Europe for a century and pushed prices up across the continent. From 1565 the Manila galleon linked Acapulco to China, closing the first global trade circuit.

The defeat of the Armada in 1588 did not end Spanish power; repeated debt defaults, the loss of the Netherlands and the War of the Spanish Succession did. The mainland American colonies broke away between 1810 and 1825. What was left went in 1898, when Cuba, Puerto Rico, the Philippines and Guam passed to the United States under the Treaty of Paris of 10 December, the conventional closing date, though Spain kept African territory until 1975.
